title: Review: Friction; Springs and Hooke's law; Angular measures and uniform circular motion; Centripetal force
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: C01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; D05-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D06-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; C02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C01-1#N.10a, C02-1#N.15, D05-1#N.11a, D06-1#N.4b, C01-1#N.12b, C02-1#N.11, D05-1#N.7b, D06-1#N.12, C01-1#N.4b, C02-1#N.8c, D06-1#N.2a, C02-1#N.4b. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Centripetal acceleration
items.clue: Rate of change of velocity in circular motion, pointing inward, of size v²/r.

items.label: Relative motion
items.clue: Movement of one surface judged against the other surface, not against the ground.

items.label: Hooke's law
items.clue: Statement that the pull of a spring is proportional to how far it has been stretched.

items.label: Centripetal force
items.clue: Inward mv²/r needed for circular motion, supplied by a real pull such as that of a string.

questions.stem: A car moves around a circular track of radius 12 m. At one instant its speed is 6.0 m/s, and its speed is increasing at a rate of 4.0 m/s². What is the magnitude of the car's acceleration at that instant?

A car drives at constant speed over the top of a rounded hill in the road. Near the top, the road's vertical cross-section is a circular arc. The car stays in contact with the road. At the top, how does the normal force from the road compare with the car's weight?

options.text: It equals the weight, since at the top the car moves neither up nor down.
It is greater than the weight, as when the car drives through a dip.
It is less than the weight, so the forces on it add to a downward force.
It equals the weight plus mv²/r, to balance an outward force.

questions.explanation: The centre of the arc is below the car, so the forces must add up to mv²/r downwards: weight − normal force = mv²/r. The normal force is less than the weight by mv²/r.

questions.stem: A book lies on the flat bed of a pickup truck. The truck speeds up from rest along a straight, level road, and the book does not slide on the bed. Which statement about friction on the book is correct?

options.text: Friction pushes the book backward, opposite to its motion.
No friction acts, since the book does not slide on the bed.
Kinetic friction from the bed pushes the book forward, as the book moves along the road.
Static friction from the bed pushes the book forward.

questions.stem: A block on a level surface with negligible friction is attached to two identical ideal springs; the other end of each spring is fixed to a wall, one on each side of the block. When the block is at its equilibrium position, both springs have their relaxed lengths. The block is pulled a distance d to the right and released from rest. Which statement describes the forces exerted on the block by the two springs just after it is released?

options.text: They point in opposite directions and add up to zero.
Both point to the left, toward the block's equilibrium position.
Both point to the right, the direction of the displacement.
Both are zero, as the block is at rest at that instant.

questions.stem: A rider on a large amusement ride moves at constant speed in a horizontal circle of radius 16 m. The ride completes 3 revolutions every 30 s. What is the magnitude of the rider's acceleration?

A highway curve is banked so that a car moving at 25 m/s can round it with no friction force from the road. Another car rounds the same curve at a constant 15 m/s without sliding. Air resistance and rolling friction are negligible. Which statement describes the static friction force exerted by the road on this slower car?

options.text: It is directed down the slope of the road, toward the center of the curve.
It is directed along the road, opposite to the direction of the car's velocity.
It is zero, since the car's tires do not slide on the road surface.
It is directed up the slope of the road, away from the center of the curve.

questions.stem: A 0.80 kg box rests on a level floor. The coefficients of friction between the box and the floor are μ_s = 0.60 and μ_k = 0.35. A student pushes the box horizontally, increasing the push slowly from zero. Use g = 10 m/s². What is the magnitude of the push when the box starts to slide?
A spring that obeys Hooke's law is 15.0 cm long when it supports a 3.0 N load and 18.0 cm long when it supports a 6.0 N load. What is its natural (unloaded) length?
questions.explanation: The extra 3.0 N adds 3.0 cm, so the extension is 1.0 cm per newton. With 3.0 N on, the extension is 3.0 cm: natural length = 15.0 − 3.0 = 12.0 cm.

questions.stem: A runner jogs at a constant speed around a circular track, completing each lap in time T. She then jogs around a second circular track with 4 times the radius of the first, at twice her original speed. By what factor is the time for one lap multiplied?

A toy car moves around the inside of a vertical circular loop of track with a diameter of 0.80 m. Friction is negligible. What is the minimum speed the car must have at the top of the loop to stay in contact with the track there? Use g = 10 m/s².

An ideal spring has a relaxed length of 10 cm. When it is stretched to a length of 14 cm, it exerts a force of magnitude 3.0 N on the object attached to it. What is the magnitude of the force it exerts when it is stretched to a length of 22 cm?

A car travels at constant speed around a curve on a flat horizontal road; its path is part of a horizontal circle. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement about the horizontal forces on the car is correct?

options.text: Friction from the road acts toward the center and is the net force.
Friction acts toward the center and is balanced by a centrifugal force.
Friction and a separate centripetal force both act toward the center.
A forward driving force along the curve is the net force on the car.

questions.explanation: On a flat road the only horizontal force toward the center is friction between the tires and the road. At constant speed no force is needed along the path, so this friction is the net force and provides mv²/r.
